# Events

The events on the app's timeline. In the app, click a dot on the timeline or an event in the Live list: the camera flies there and the event card opens.

## 800 BC · Villanovan village by the Arno ford

*Orsanmichele*

Before Florence there were Iron Age (Villanovan) villages on the plain by the Arno ford: oval huts, some on stilts, with hearths, pottery kilns and animal pens; the dead were cremated and buried in urns to the west, under today’s Via Strozzi. The layout shown is inferred from the finds.

Sources: [A07 – Villanovan / Etruscan Florence (web syntheses)](https://www.florencecity.it/la-firenze-villanoviana-ed-etrusca/); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civiltà_villanoviana)

## 700 BC · Orientalizing hut between Badia and Bargello

*Badia – Bargello*

Excavations between the Badia and the Bargello found the floor of a hut with Orientalizing pottery (7th c. BC), some of it imported from Asia Minor – a sign of trade along the river long before the Roman town.

Sources: [A07 – Villanovan / Etruscan Florence (web syntheses)](https://www.florencecity.it/la-firenze-villanoviana-ed-etrusca/); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badia_Fiorentina)

## 59 BC · Foundation of Florentia (traditional date)

*Castrum*

Tradition dates the Roman colony of Florentia to 59 BC, under Caesar; archaeology points to c. 30–15 BC. A castrum with a grid of streets, the forum where Piazza della Repubblica is today, walls, baths and a theatre.

Sources: [A03 – Comune di Firenze, archaeological data](https://opendata.comune.fi.it/); [History notes (H sources)](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florentia)

## 8 September 1296 · Foundation stone of Santa Maria del Fiore

*Duomo*

On 8 September 1296 the first stone of the new cathedral was laid; Arnolfo di Cambio designed it to replace the old church of Santa Reparata, which was taken down as the new building grew over it.

Sources: [M04 – Duomo landmark model](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/landmarks/DUOMO.md); [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattedrale_di_Santa_Maria_del_Fiore)

## 4 November 1333 · Great flood of the Arno

*Arno*

On 4 November 1333 the Arno flooded the city and carried away the Ponte Vecchio, Ponte alla Carraia and Ponte Santa Trinita; the Ponte Vecchio was rebuilt in stone by 1345.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvione_di_Firenze_del_1333)

## 1348 · Black Death

*City-wide*

The plague of 1348 killed perhaps half of Florence’s population; work on many buildings slowed for years. Boccaccio set the Decameron in that year.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peste_nera)

## 25 March 1436 · Consecration of the Duomo with Brunelleschi’s dome

*Duomo*

Pope Eugene IV consecrated Santa Maria del Fiore on 25 March 1436, the Florentine New Year. Brunelleschi’s dome, built 1420–36 without centring, was closed; the lantern followed 1446–61.

Sources: [M04 – Duomo landmark model](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/landmarks/DUOMO.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cupola_del_Brunelleschi)

## 26 April 1478 · Pazzi conspiracy

*Duomo*

On Sunday 26 April 1478, during Mass in the cathedral, the Pazzi and their allies attacked Lorenzo and Giuliano de’ Medici: Giuliano was killed, Lorenzo escaped to the sacristy. The conspirators were hanged from the windows of Palazzo Vecchio.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congiura_dei_Pazzi)

## 7 February 1497 · Bonfire of the Vanities

*Piazza della Signoria*

On 7 February 1497, carnival Tuesday, Savonarola’s followers burned mirrors, cosmetics, books, paintings and fine clothes on a great pyre in Piazza della Signoria.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falò_delle_vanità)

## 23 May 1498 · Execution of Savonarola

*Piazza della Signoria*

On 23 May 1498 Girolamo Savonarola and two of his friars were hanged and burned in Piazza della Signoria, where a round plaque in the paving marks the place today.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girolamo_Savonarola)

## 14 May 1504 · The David leaves the Opera del Duomo

*Opera del Duomo → Piazza della Signoria*

On 14 May 1504 Michelangelo’s David left the Opera del Duomo yard through a breach in the wall, slung inside a timber frame that rolled on greased beams, pulled and pushed by over 40 men. The ≈600 m to Piazza della Signoria took four days. The route shown is presumed.

Sources: [Opera di Santa Maria del Fiore – Quando il David si mosse](https://duomo.firenze.it/it/opera-magazine/post/4693/quando-il-david-si-mosse); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_(Michelangelo))

## 8 June 1504 · The David set on the ringhiera

*Piazza della Signoria*

On 8 June 1504 the David was raised onto the ringhiera by the palace door, where Donatello’s Judith had stood; it was unveiled on 8 September 1504.

Sources: [Opera di Santa Maria del Fiore – Quando il David si mosse](https://duomo.firenze.it/it/opera-magazine/post/4693/quando-il-david-si-mosse); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_(Michelangelo))

## 1873 · The David moved to the Accademia

*Piazza della Signoria → Galleria dell’Accademia*

In 1873 the original David was taken indoors to the Galleria dell’Accademia to protect it from the weather; the square stayed without it until the marble copy of 1910.

Sources: [M06 – Palazzo Vecchio landmark model](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/landmarks/PALAZZO-VECCHIO.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_(Michelangelo))

## 1910 · A marble copy of the David in Piazza della Signoria

*Piazza della Signoria*

Since 1910 a marble copy stands at the original place by the door of Palazzo Vecchio.

Sources: [M06 – Palazzo Vecchio landmark model](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/landmarks/PALAZZO-VECCHIO.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_(Michelangelo))

## 17 February 1530 · Calcio during the siege

*Piazza Santa Croce*

On 17 February 1530, with the imperial army besieging the city, the Florentines played a match of calcio in Piazza Santa Croce in open defiance, musicians on the roof of the church.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Events & costumes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/EVENTS-COSTUMES.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcio_storico_fiorentino)

## 14 May 1550 · A market morning in Mercato Vecchio

*Mercato Vecchio*

The Mercato Vecchio, on the site of the Roman forum, was the city’s daily food market for centuries, around the Colonna dell’Abbondanza, until it was demolished in the Risanamento of 1885–95.

Sources: [H11 – Risanamento](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercato_Vecchio_(Firenze))

## 27 March 1622 · Scoppio del Carro – the new Brindellone

*Piazza del Duomo*

On Easter Sunday a mechanical dove (the colombina) runs along a wire from the high altar of the Duomo and sets off the fireworks on the cart, the Brindellone, outside the door; a good flight promises a good harvest. The cart still in use was built in 1622.

Sources: [Events & costumes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/EVENTS-COSTUMES.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoppio_del_carro)

## 1865 · Florence capital of Italy · walls demolished (Poggi plan)

*Viali*

From 1865 to 1871 Florence was the capital of the Kingdom of Italy. Giuseppe Poggi’s plan pulled down the northern walls for the ring of viali, kept the gates standing alone, and built the Piazzale Michelangelo.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firenze_capitale)

## 1888 · Mercato Vecchio & ghetto demolished

*Piazza della Repubblica*

In the Risanamento (1885–95) the Mercato Vecchio, the old ghetto and the medieval streets around them were demolished; Piazza della Repubblica with its arcade and porticoes took their place.

Sources: [H11 – Risanamento](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risanamento_di_Firenze)

## 3 August 1944 · The Night of the Bridges

*Arno*

From the evening of 3 August to dawn on 4 August 1944 the retreating German army blew up every bridge over the Arno except the Ponte Vecchio, and mined the houses at both of its ends to block the approaches.

Sources: [Events & costumes (La Nazione, Uffizi, storiadifirenze.org)](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/EVENTS-COSTUMES.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battaglia_di_Firenze)

## 4 November 1966 · The great flood

*Santa Croce*

On 4 November 1966 the Arno came over the parapets of the lungarni before dawn, broke them on the Lungarno Corsini and at Piazza Cavalleggeri, and ran through the streets: 4.92 m on the plaque in Via dei Neri, Piazza del Duomo under water by 9:45. It began to fall at 8 p.m. and left the streets on the 6th. Cimabue’s Crucifix, the Gates of Paradise and thousands of books and works of art were damaged; volunteers from all over the world, the "angeli del fango", came to help. The live scene shows the water rising hour by hour.

Sources: [History notes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/HISTORY.md); [Lungarni and the flood (model notes)](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/landmarks/LUNGARNI.md#the-flood-of-4-november-1966); [Protezione Civile: the flood of Florence](https://servizio-nazionale.protezionecivile.gov.it/static/4019da085c64ebd948af0693ce73176e/alluvione-firenze.pdf); [1966 flood of the Arno (en.wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1966_flood_of_the_Arno); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvione_di_Firenze_del_4_novembre_1966)

## 5 April 2026 · Scoppio del Carro (Easter)

*Piazza del Duomo*

Today the fire for the Scoppio is still struck from the flints of the Holy Sepulchre kept at Santi Apostoli; the colombina flies at 11 on Easter morning.

Sources: [Events & costumes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/EVENTS-COSTUMES.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoppio_del_carro)

## 24 June 2026 · Calcio Storico final (San Giovanni)

*Piazza Santa Croce*

Revived in 1930, the calcio storico is played in Piazza Santa Croce each June between the four quarters; the final falls on 24 June, the feast of San Giovanni.

Sources: [Events & costumes](https://github.com/Jany-M/firenze-story/blob/main/docs/EVENTS-COSTUMES.md); [Wikipedia](https://it.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcio_storico_fiorentino)
